findings.title: Combining auth and filter SQL loses grouping when filter has top-level OR
findings.body: getBaseConditions wraps both parts in parentheses, which is fine. But the reduce joins in buildFilterConditions (line 121) and the OR joins in the auth builders build on fragments such as `("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)` that are unparenthesised at the top level. Within the reduce the accumulator is wrapped, so it is correct today. The auth condition returned directly from getAuthorizationConditions (e.g. an OR at top level) is unsafe if any caller embeds it without wrapping it in parentheses, because AND/OR precedence would then widen the result set and leak bookings across scopes. Each builder should return a self-parenthesised fragment.

findings.title: Org scope drops user clause when org has no child teams
findings.body: userIdsFromOrg is only queried when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. An org with no child teams therefore gets no personal-booking clause, even though org members' non-team bookings would otherwise be included. This is the same as the old behaviour, but it is now baked into the SQL and is inconsistent with the team-scope builder.

findings.title: Team scope behaviour changed and the test no longer covers an empty team
findings.body: The team scope now omits the user clause when the team has no members. Previously it emitted `userId IN []`. This is semantically fine, but the changed branch has no test.

findings.title: Caching tests removed and DB test queries a view without a type cast
findings.body: The caching tests were deleted although the service still caches the auth and filter conditions, so that behaviour is now untested. The raw-query test also relies on parameters like `ANY(${array})` binding correctly to integer columns; this is unverified, and the PR admits the tests were never run.
